JinkoCommitFlightRefundConfig.description: Refund or void a booked flight (every ticket on the item) against a quote the customer accepted

booking_ref.description: Jinko booking reference. Call get_booking first, then select its booked_item_id for servicing.
booking_ref.title: Booking Ref

booked_item_id.description: The booked item, from get_booking items[].booked_item_id. Preserved across exchanges. Omit only when the booking has exactly one item of the requested domain; otherwise a 409 returns items to choose from.
booked_item_id.title: Booked Item Id

last_name.description: Required for guest lookup. A credential that owns the booking may omit it; ownership is checked by the platform.
last_name.title: Last Name

quote_id.description: The `quote_id` from a preceding POST /v1/flight_refund_preview. Binds this commit to the figures that quote reported.
quote_id.title: Quote Id

acknowledged.description: The refund the customer was shown — copy the preview's `refund.amount_money` across. Copying the whole `refund` object, as older integrations do, is still accepted. REQUIRED whenever the preview carried a `refund`, which is every quote that names a figure. It may be omitted in exactly one case: a MANUAL_REQUIRED quote that carries no `refund` at all because the penalty is unknown (`penalty.fee_known: false`), submitted with `manual_ok: true` — there is no figure to acknowledge, and inventing one would have the customer agree to a number nobody computed. Omitting it anywhere else is refused by the platform, not here. When present, all three of `value` (minor units), `currency` and `decimal_places` are required: the platform compares this against the refund as it stands, and a figure whose scale is unstated cannot be compared. `amount` is not accepted in its place. Any other key, such as `display` or `basis`, is ignored. A mismatch against a still-live quote’s refund is answered 409 `quote_drift`. `retry_quote_id` is that same quote’s handle and `current.refund` its figure. Show it to the customer, then commit again with that handle and figure. Nothing is sent to the airline.

manual_ok.description: Send `true` to submit a quote whose `support_level` is MANUAL_REQUIRED. The operation is then raised for a Jinko agent and answers `state: attention_required` with `reason: manual_required` — NOTHING is sent to the airline by this call, and the agent settles or fails it. Without the flag such a commit is refused 409 `manual_required`, so a customer is never put in an agent queue unasked. On an AUTO or AUTO_VOID quote the flag changes nothing. This is also the one submission that may carry no `acknowledged` figure — when the quote itself named none, because the penalty is unknown.
manual_ok.title: Manual Ok

value.description: Integer amount in MINOR units, always paired with decimal_places — divide by 10 ** decimal_places to display. Example: value 15977 with decimal_places 2 is 159.77 USD. Rendering this field directly shows prices 100x too high for 2-decimal currencies.
value.title: Value

decimal_places.description: Scale of the integer value/amount: display = integer / 10 ** decimal_places. Always sent alongside minor-unit amounts. Usually the ISO 4217 digits of the currency (2 for USD/EUR/GBP, 0 for JPY/KRW, 3 for BHD/JOD/KWD) but currency-converted prices can carry a different scale — ALWAYS use the decimal_places sent with the amount, never a hardcoded 2. Only if the field is genuinely absent on a value-shaped object, fall back to the ISO digits for the currency.
decimal_places.title: Decimal Places

email.description: Contact email for booking confirmations. A trip with a flight needs it before payment: without a contact email, checkout answers 422 `MISSING_CUSTOMER_DETAILS` with `email` in `missing_fields`.

phone.description: Contact phone in international format: a leading `+` and country code, e.g. `+12025550147`. Spaces, hyphens, dots and parentheses are accepted and removed. A number without the leading `+` is rejected with `INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER`. Required to complete a booking.
phone.title: Phone

title.description: Honorific of the booking contact (e.g. "mr", "ms", "mx"). Free text, resolved downstream per provider. Required to book a car rental; optional otherwise.
title.title: Title

flight_number.description: The driver's arriving flight for a CAR rental, as an IATA flight designator: a two- or three-character airline code then 1 to 4 digits and an optional letter (`BA472`, `AF1234`, `RUS1727`). Spaces and hyphens are accepted and removed; a value that is not a designator is rejected with `INVALID_FLIGHT_NUMBER`. Always optional — a car offer's `pick_up.requires_flight_number` says whether the rental desk asks for one, and a quote lists `flight_number` in that item's required details, but no branch policy blocks checkout without it. Supply it when you have it: the rental company can then hold the car for a delayed flight. Ignored by flights, hotels and ground.

airline.description: IATA code of the loyalty program issuer (e.g. `LH` for Lufthansa Miles & More), not necessarily the operating carrier — alliances credit miles on partner flights.

number.title: Number

special_requests.description: HOTEL ITEMS ONLY. Free-text special requests for the property, one per entry — late arrival, quiet room, high floor, bedding preference, non-smoking room, baby cot, accessibility needs. They apply to the whole stay and are forwarded to the hotel supplier with the booking as REQUESTS ONLY: neither Jinko nor the supplier guarantees them, and a confirmed booking does not mean the hotel will honour them. At most 10 entries of 500 characters each and 1500 characters in total, counted after trimming; blank entries are dropped. Ignored on flight and ground items. Echoed back on the item as `special_requests`, trimmed and without the blank entries (JIN-2499).
examples: A quiet room on a high floor, if available.

first_name.description: For flights, the airline must be able to print the name on the ticket: Latin letters (accents allowed), spaces, hyphens and apostrophes only. The last name holds at most 29 characters (the airline cannot ticket a longer surname), and first, middle and last name together at most 63. Two travellers in one trip cannot share the same full name. A name that breaks these rules is refused at upsert_travelers or checkout with 400 BAD_REQUEST and `error.field` naming the traveller.
first_name.title: First Name

last_name.description: For flights, the airline must be able to print the name on the ticket: Latin letters (accents allowed), spaces, hyphens and apostrophes only. The last name holds at most 29 characters (the airline cannot ticket a longer surname), and first, middle and last name together at most 63. Two travellers in one trip cannot share the same full name. A name that breaks these rules is refused at upsert_travelers or checkout with 400 BAD_REQUEST and `error.field` naming the traveller.
last_name.title: Last Name

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD, nothing before or after it). Required for flights, and for a `child` or `infant` staying at a hotel; optional for an adult on a hotel-only trip. For flights it cannot be in the future and must agree with `traveler_type` on the trip's flight dates; otherwise upsert_travelers or checkout answers 400 BAD_REQUEST with `error.field` naming the traveller and field.
date_of_birth.title: Date Of Birth

gender.description: Required for flights; optional for hotel-only trips. Accepted in either case (`male` reads as `MALE`).
gender.title: Gender

traveler_type.description: Accepted in either case (`Adult` reads as `adult`). For flights, the traveller's age on the date the booking ages travellers on decides the type — the trip's first flight, or for some bookings the return flight of a round trip: `adult` 12 or older, `child` 2 to 11, `infant` under 2, and an `infant` must still be under 2 on the trip's last flight. A type the `date_of_birth` contradicts is refused at upsert_travelers (once the trip holds the flight) or at checkout with 400 BAD_REQUEST and `error.field` naming the traveller. A flight searched for another party is re-priced for these travellers at checkout, on the same flights and fare family; when that fare is not sold for them, checkout answers 409 `OFFER_UNAVAILABLE`. Each hotel in the trip is booked with these travellers (a `room_bundle` hotel whose rooms `hotel_room_guests` names is booked for those room guests instead), so they cannot name more adults or more children than its rooms were priced for (the hotel_search `occupancies`: `adults` and `children_ages`), and each child's age at check-in must be one of the priced `children_ages`. The hotel counts a traveller by age at check-in, 18 or older being an adult, and a traveller with no `date_of_birth` as an adult. upsert_travelers or checkout answers 400 BAD_REQUEST naming the first traveller over a count or with an age the room was not priced for; search the hotel again for the party.
traveler_type.title: Traveler Type

passport_expiry.description: Passport expiry (YYYY-MM-DD, nothing before or after it). For flights it cannot be before the trip's last flight; otherwise upsert_travelers or checkout answers 400 BAD_REQUEST with `error.field` naming the traveller.
passport_expiry.title: Passport Expiry

known_traveler_number.description: US trusted-traveler Known Traveler Number (TSA PreCheck / Global Entry). Flights only; sent to the airline as Secure Flight data so PreCheck eligibility prints on the boarding pass.
known_traveler_number.title: Known Traveler Number

known_traveler_issuing_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country that issued the Known Traveler Number. Defaults to `US` downstream; ignored without known_traveler_number.
known_traveler_issuing_country.title: Known Traveler Issuing Country

redress_number.description: DHS redress control number (TRIP program). Flights only; sent to the airline as Secure Flight data.
redress_number.title: Redress Number

redress_issuing_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country that issued the redress number. Defaults to `US` downstream; ignored without redress_number.
redress_issuing_country.title: Redress Issuing Country
